Let me think about the GITHUB_TOKEN issue. The `just up` command requires `GITHUB_TOKEN` as a preflight check. Let me understand what the token is actually used for.

Looking at the flow:
1. `just up` → `node scripts/urbo/up.mjs`
2. Preflight checks: docker, node, pnpm, just, docker daemon, proxy port, GITHUB_TOKEN
3. Then it does `pnpm install` in app/, starts dev servers, builds containers (which builds the backend image via `compose create --build`)

The backend Dockerfile (docker/spring/Dockerfile) mounts the github_token as a secret and uses it in `./gradlew bootJar`. The Gradle build needs GITHUB_TOKEN to pull packages from GitHub packages.

Actually the compose secret `github_token` is required by the `spring-app` build. If GITHUB_TOKEN env is not set, the secret will be empty, and `GITHUB_TOKEN="$(cat /run/secrets/github_token)"` will be empty. Then `./gradlew bootJar` runs without the token. Whether that succeeds depends on whether Gradle needs the token.

But the preflight check will fail first, so `just up` will never even reach the build. So even if the build could work without the token, the preflight gates it.
